faqs.a:
(a)
Application.
The owner of any property who:
(1)
Prior to August 3, 1981, installed one or more public improvements may file with the
               city manager an application for a reimbursement district on a form provided by the
               city. The application shall include the nature, location, and cost of the improvements,
               a description of the proposed district and individual properties within it, the names
               and addresses of the property owners within the district, the proposed manner of assessment
               and the amount proposed to be assessed against each property for each improvement.
(2)
Proposes to install one or more public improvements may file with the city manager
               an application for a reimbursement district on a form provided by the city. The application
               shall include the nature, location and anticipated cost of the improvements, a description
               of the proposed district and individual properties within it, the names and addresses
               of the property owners within the district, the proposed manner of assessment and
               the amount proposed to be assessed against each property for each improvement. With
               respect to public improvements, construction of which commences after August 3, 1981,
               the application shall be accompanied by three construction bids.
(b)
Notice.
A notice shall be mailed to the owners of each property within the proposed district
               together with a copy of the application. The notice shall state that any owner may
               file a written request for an administrative hearing to contest the proposal. The
               request for hearing shall state in general terms the grounds of objection.
(c)
Hearing.
The city manager shall schedule a hearing and notify the applicant and all objecting
               parties. The city manager or his designee shall conduct the hearing in accordance
               with the city Code provisions pertaining to the conduct of quasi-judicial hearings.
(d)
Advisory decision.
After the hearing, the presiding officer shall render an advisory decision summarizing
               the objections and making recommendations to the city council.
(e)
Adoption of ordinance.
After the hearing or if no hearing is requested, the city council shall then consider
               the adoption of an ordinance establishing a reimbursement district and imposing appropriate
               assessments which shall be liens upon the property assessed. A notice of the lien
               shall be filed in the office of the county clerk and recorded.
(f)
Judicial review.
Any reimbursement assessment ordinance adopted hereunder shall be subject to judicial
               review pursuant to Colorado Rule of Civil Procedure No. 106.
(Code 1981, § 27-185; Ord. No. 1721, § 5, 2-2-1981; Ord. No. 1764, § 4, 8-3-1981;
               Ord. No. 1805, § 3, 1-4-1982)
